components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type

          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors

          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title

        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors

      title: Validation message

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"

## Summary

I implemented the `locality` field on owner creation. When an owner is created, the response now includes `locality` set to `"local"` if their city is the single most common city among existing owners at that moment, otherwise `"remote"`.

Changes:
- **`openapi.yml`** — added the read-only `locality` property to the `Owner` schema (the `OwnerDto` is regenerated from this at build time).
- **`Owner.java`** — added a `@Transient locality` field with getter/setter, matching the existing pattern for `namesakeCount`/`sharesHousehold`.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — in `addOwner`, set `owner.setLocality(resolveLocality(owner.getCity()))` before persisting, and added the `resolveLocality` helper. It groups existing owners by normalized city, finds the highest count, and returns `"local"` only when exactly one city holds that max and it matches the new owner's city; ties, brand-new cities, and an empty owner set all yield `"remote"`. City matching reuses the existing `normalize` helper, so it's case/whitespace-insensitive like the rest of the controller.
- MapStruct auto-maps `locality` (matching property names), consistent with the other computed fields.

New tests in `OwnerRestControllerV1Tests` cover: most-common city (`Madison` → local), case-insensitive match (`madison` → local), a less-common city (`Monona` → remote), and a brand-new city (`Boston` → remote).
